title: Carbon footprint of electricity generation

author.literal: UK Parliamentary Office of Science and Technology

publisher: Parliamentary Office of Science and Technology, UK Parliament

backsClaims: The true origin of FUEL_FACTORS oil 650, via Electricity Maps
custom.caveat: Verbatim: 'The average carbon footprint of oil-fired electricity generation plants in the UK is ~650gCO2eq/kWh.' This is a UK-fleet average from 2006 for a fuel supplying 1% of UK generation. It's neither a global median nor an IPCC figure. parliament.uk returns 403 to automated clients; retrieved via the Wayback Machine. POST's own solar (58) and wind (4.64/5.25) figures don't match what this repo uses, so only the oil row travelled.

title: Default emission factors (config/defaults.yaml)

backsClaims: The proximate source of this project's former factor table, including the solar 45 that proved it was a copy
custom.caveat: Publishes solar 45 under the label 'IPCC 2014'. 45 appears nowhere in AR5; it's the rounded mean of the AR5 rooftop (41) and utility (48) rows, i.e. Electricity Maps' own editorial choice presented as an IPCC value. This project carried 45 until 2026-08-23, which is what proved its table was copied from here rather than read out of AR5; it now uses the AR5 utility row, 48. Electricity Maps has no lignite or waste mode at all, so those two values came from somewhere else again.

custom.caveat: The midpoint match is exact but gives no evidence the repo derived 1050 this way. Note also that 1050 is this review's upper bound for HARD coal, so a transcription slip is equally plausible. Cited only as the best available published range for lignite.

title: A Changing Climate for Energy from Waste? Final Report for Friends of the Earth
publisher: Eunomia Research & Consulting, for Friends of the Earth

backsClaims: The true origin of FUEL_FACTORS waste 580
custom.caveat: Table 1 gives 580 gCO2eq/kWh for an electricity-only incinerator in the FUTURE modelled scenario (current was 510), EXCLUDING biogenic carbon. Including biogenic carbon the same row is 1405. So the repo's 580 is a UK 2006 scenario figure for direct fossil-only emissions, being used in a table labelled 'lifecycle medians'. Wrong on source, vintage and system boundary at once. Retrieved via the Wayback Machine.

title: Carbon Intensity Forecast Methodology

custom.caveat: These are DIRECT gCO2/kWh factors with lifecycle CO2eq excluded: hydro, nuclear, solar and wind are all scored 0. Mixing the 'Other 300' row into a lifecycle table is a system-boundary error. Note also that this table's oil is 935 while the repo uses 650, so the repo did not take oil from the API it actually reads.

title: Global Electricity Review 2026

custom.caveat: Verbatim: 'The emissions intensity of electricity has dropped 14% over the last decade, from 533 grams of CO2 equivalent per kWh (gCO2e/kWh) in 2015 to 458 gCO2e/kWh in 2025.' Chosen over the better-known IEA figure because it's CO2-equivalent and incorporates IPCC lifecycle intensities, so it shares a system boundary with FUEL_FACTORS. PDF fetched and searched directly on 2026-08-23.

title: Electricity 2026

backsClaims: Establishes that the widely-quoted IEA global average is 435 gCO2/kWh for 2025, and that it's a DIRECT figure with lifecycle emissions excluded
custom.caveat: Verbatim: 'the improvement in global CO2 intensity has been significant, declining by 14% to 435 g CO2/kWh in 2025.' IEA's own documentation states 'the intensities corresponding to renewable sources (including biofuels) and nuclear are equal to zero', which is definitionally not a lifecycle factor. Cited here to explain why this repo avoids the IEA number. A search of the report for '450 g' returns nothing, so the repo's former 450 was not an IEA figure either.

The authors are WattTime-affiliated and WattTime's own model is the one their proposed tests favour, which should be disclosed wherever this is cited.

custom.caveat: Page read directly on 2026-08-23; it states its own last update as 2026-08-04 and uses eGRID2022 vintage data. All three constants in this repo had drifted from it. The tree figure is the one most often misused: EPA defines it as a survival-weighted average over the first ten years of a newly planted medium-growth urban seedling, and states the figure is 'not appropriate for reforestation projects'. It isn't a mature tree's annual rate. EPA publishes no per-kilometre figure, so that conversion is ours.
